comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Done. The core grew crates/muster-core/src/attention.rs - window focus plus seen-ness per pane - and the seam grew one request, WindowFocus, which is the only thing about attention the shell can see and the core cannot.

The decision worth recording: herdr's own `done` is normalized back to idle on the way in rather than trusted alongside ours. It is derived from a client-focus signal it can never get from us, so keeping it would mean two writers for one field with no way to tell whose answer is on screen - the failure architecture.md already names. Ours is the writer that can see the window.

The open question on this card is answered the only way it can be, and stated in the module doc rather than hidden: `done` means 'nobody we know of saw it'. A second Muster window or a herdr TUI beside us is focus we cannot observe.

Cases in corpus/conformance/attention.json (14, authored). The end-to-end proof is in crates/muster-seam/tests/attach.rs, and the assertion that cannot pass by accident is the settling one - herdr never revises its answer when a Muster window gains focus, because it cannot see that happen.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
herdr computes `done` as idle-on-an-unseen-pane, and seen-ness reads the foreground
client's window focus, which its JSON API has no method for (a_26LAtaO6T, parked). The
consequence is not cosmetic: an agent that finishes while a Muster window sits unfocused
reads `idle` rather than `done`, and attention routing is why this project exists.

Muster already holds both halves. The agent channel delivers every working -> idle
transition to the core, and the shell is the only thing that knows whether its own window
had OS focus at that moment. `done` is a claim about whether anyone saw the pane, and no
daemon can answer that for a window it cannot see.

So this is ordinary work we own rather than a favor to wait on, and it costs a desideratum
nothing if herdr never moves. architecture.md already allows for it: state is daemon truth,
but one of the five is computed from a client-side input, so the vocabulary carries that
input.

What does not exist yet is the input. The shell has to report window focus across the seam,
and the core has to hold seen-ness per pane - which pane was visible, in a focused window,
at the moment its agent went idle.

Open: what a second Muster window, or a herdr TUI attached beside us, does to the answer.
Ours is the only focus we can observe, so `done` becomes "nobody *we know of* saw it".
title: 🎯 Compute `done` ourselves, instead of asking herdr for focus
